page: Amazon Web Services r8i.48xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It is powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors featuring an x86_64 architecture with 96 physical cores, 192 vCPUs via two threads per core, and a peak clock frequency of 3.9 GHz. Cache resources include 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 480 MB L3 cache pool. Hardware-level instruction support includes AVX-512, Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions) for matrix math acceleration, and hardware cryptography instructions such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

System memory consists of 1,536 GB of high-speed DDR5 RAM rated at 7,000 MT/s, yielding a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include local instance storage, requiring network-attached Amazon EBS storage configurations for persistence. Integrated network connectivity offers up to 75 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth, accommodating heavy data transmission across external nodes.

Benchmark measurements highlight strong parallel computing and memory throughput capabilities. Multi-core performance metrics, such as the stress-ng multi-core CPU score (207,544.22) and Geekbench multi-core score (21,917.0), rank in the top 10 percent of evaluated systems, alongside high uncached read memory bandwidth reaching 573.74 GB/sec. The presence of AMX instructions enables high prompt processing throughput in CPU-based LLM benchmarks (4,152.24 tokens/sec on 135M models and 330.07 tokens/sec on 7B models), although sequential token generation rates reflect standard CPU inference constraints. Single-threaded benchmarks, such as stress-ng single-core (2,121.39), settle in the median range.

Given its massive memory allocation and high multi-threaded compute density, r8i.48xlarge delivers qualitative operational cost efficiency for consolidated, memory-heavy architectures. Primary tradeoffs involve the complete absence of bundled local storage and moderate single-core instruction throughput. The instance is specifically suited for massive in-memory databases like Redis, extensive data warehousing, enterprise relational database systems, large-scale Clang compilation jobs, and distributed data processing frameworks.
description: Amazon Web Services r8i.48xlarge is a memory-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro System. It is equipped with 192 vCPUs across 96 physical cores powered by Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors clocked at 3.9 GHz, accompanied by 480 MB of L3 cache and support for AMX and AVX-512 instructions. Memory capacity stands at 1,536 GB of DDR5 RAM operating at 7 GHz, delivering an 8 GB per vCPU ratio alongside 75 Gbps of baseline network throughput. The instance lacks bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage solutions. Benchmark data demonstrates top-tier multi-threaded processing, robust memory read/write bandwidth, and high throughput in database and prompt processing operations, while single-core performance remains average. The r8i.48xlarge is designed for large in-memory databases, real-time analytics, intensive batch processing, and high-concurrency enterprise workloads.
